title: Access & Residency Exception Request Process (ARERP)
author: Maya Chen
body:
Overview:

Purpose:
This document defines the Access & Residency Exception Request Process (ARERP) used by Redwood Inference teams to request, evaluate, approve, monitor, and revoke exceptions to RBAC, data residency, and retention policies. ARERP ensures exceptions are timeboxed, risk-assessed, and evidence-backed so the company maintains auditability and minimal exposure.

Scope:
- Temporary changes to role assignments that grant expanded privileges (RBAC exceptions)
- Requests to store or process data in locations outside standard residency zones (Residency exceptions)
- Deviations from documented retention schedules for specific datasets (Retention exceptions)
- Any exception that affects audit logging posture or requires changes to collection/retention of logs

Actors and Responsibilities:
- Requester: Individual or team initiating the exception (owner must be a manager-level engineer or product lead).
- Security Reviewer: Security team member who performs risk assessments and recommends controls.
- Data Privacy Lead: Evaluates residency and legal/regulatory constraints.
- Approver: Designated approver(s) depending on risk tier (see Decision Matrix).
- System Owner: Service/account owner responsible for implementing and reverting changes.
- Audit Owner: Responsible for ensuring evidence (logs, approvals) is retained.

Submission Requirements (minimum evidence):
1) Exception request form (use template below).
2) Justification and business impact analysis (why required, user/customer impact).
3) Duration requested (start/end dates).
4) Exact scope of privileges or dataset identifiers (resource ARNs / project IDs).
5) Proposed compensating controls (least-privilege narrowing, session timeouts, elevated access via jumpbox, step-up auth).
6) Audit evidence plan: which logs will be captured, retention window, retention location.
7) Data residency impact: countries/regions, contractual/regulatory notes, any DPA or customer-specific requirements.
8) Rollback plan and verification steps.

Decision Matrix and Risk Tiers:
- Low Risk: Non-production feature flags, ephemeral developer tooling with read-only access to non-sensitive data. Approver: Team Lead + Security Reviewer.
- Medium Risk: Changes that touch production metadata, limited write access, or residency deviation to a neighboring region. Approver: Product Manager + Data Privacy Lead + Security Reviewer.
- High Risk: Broad write/delete privileges in production, cross-border residency with legal constraints, or retention changes impacting regulated data. Approver: Head of Security + Legal + CTO.

Approval SLA and Timeboxes:
- Initial triage: security reviewer responds within 24 business hours.
- Medium-risk decision target: 3 business days.
- High-risk decision target: 7 business days.
- Maximum approved duration by default: 30 days (extensions must reapply and include a justification and new evidence).

Template: Exception Request (copy into new request ticket)
---
Title: <short description>
Requestor: <name/team>
Service / Resource(s): <service name, project id, ARNs>
Type: RBAC | Residency | Retention | Mixed
Risk Tier (requester suggestion): Low | Medium | High
Start: YYYY-MM-DD
End: YYYY-MM-DD
Justification: <reason>
Compensating Controls: <list>
Audit Plan: <logs to collect, retention location, owner>
Rollback Plan: <steps to revert>
Stakeholders: <names/emails>
Attachments: <evidence, config diffs, screenshots>
---

Compensating Controls Catalog (examples):
- Temporary session tokens with 1-hour TTL, enforced MFA
- Restricted egress via proxy/VPC endpoint and allowlist of destination IPs
- Live observability: custom dashboard for the duration, with alerting on anomalous patterns
- Query and write quotas for elevated roles
- Continuous audit stream replicated to secure S3 bucket with immutable retention policy

Audit Evidence Requirements
- All approved exceptions must be accompanied by a single JSON manifest stored in: s3://redwood-compliance/exceptions/{exception-id}.json
- Manifest fields (examples): exception_id, requester, approvers, start, end, resources, compensating_controls, evidence_location.
- Required logs: IAM policy change events, STS token issuance, data-access events (read/write/delete), network egress logs for affected hosts.
- Retain audit evidence for the longer of: approved exception duration + 90 days OR base regulatory retention period.

Operational Steps (Request -> Review -> Approve -> Revoke)
1) Requester opens an ARERP ticket in the Exceptions queue and attaches the template.
2) Security Reviewer performs a risk assessment and documents findings in the ticket (including recommended mitigations).
3) Data Privacy Lead reviews residency impact for non-US regions and flags legal constraints.
4) Approver(s) sign off in the ticket and add the exception manifest to the compliance S3 path.
5) System Owner implements changes and notifies Audit Owner who validates logs are being captured and retained.
6) During exception window, Security runs weekly checks for anomalous activity (short checklist below).
7) At end date, System Owner revokes elevated access and performs a verification runbook.
8) Audit Owner runs a reconciliation: confirm manifest, logs, and remediation evidence exist.

Weekly Security Checklist (during exception):
- Verify active sessions for elevated accounts (list).
- Confirm no write/deletes outside declared scope.
- Check network egress to non-allowlisted destinations.
- Ensure alerting thresholds are active and have fired if anomalies detected.

Revocation and Post-Mortem
- Immediate revocation criteria: unexpected data access, exfiltration indicators, elevated auth token used outside scope, or legal request from compliance/legal.
- If revocation occurs early, the Security Reviewer files an incident-security page and triggers the incident response procedures per /confluence/security-and-compliance/incident-response-security/incident-operational-playbook-2024.
- Post-exception post-mortem required for any exception that: (a) exceeded duration, (b) had a trigger causing revocation, or (c) produced any audit alerts. The post-mortem must include timeline, root cause, and corrective actions.

Periodic Review and Metrics
- Quarterly audit: Security and Internal Audit will sample a minimum of 10% of approved exceptions for full evidence completeness.
- KPIs to track: time-to-decision, number of extensions, incidents triggered during exception, and average time to revoke.

Integration with Secure SDLC
- Exceptions tied to feature rollouts must be requested in tandem with a release ticket and include test plans that validate least-privilege behaviors.
- CI/CD gates will automatically refuse deployments that rely on an active exception unless the manifest exists and approvers are listed in the ticket.

Common Scenarios and Guidance
- Developer needing temporary prod read access: suggest read-only role with session TTL and logging; mark as Low risk.
- Partner integration requiring cross-border storage for a pilot: medium risk; require Data Privacy Lead sign-off and per-customer DPAs.
- Hotfix requiring schema migration with delete privileges: high risk; recommend canary window and DB-level replication snapshot before change.

Records and Evidence Retention Table:
| Artifact | Owner | Minimum Retention |
|---|---|---|
| Exception manifest | Audit Owner | exception_end + 90 days |
| IAM change logs | System Owner / Audit | exception_end + 365 days |
| Data access logs (sensitive datasets) | Data Team / Audit | regulatory minimum (e.g., 7 years) |
| Post-mortem | Security | permanent |

Escalation and Risk Acceptance
- If approvers and stakeholders disagree, Security escalates to Head of Security and Legal for resolution within 48 hours.
- Formal risk acceptance for high-risk exceptions must be recorded in the Risk Register and include a compensating-control verification plan.

Appendices
A. Example manifest JSON (store as .json in S3)
